title: Suicide Trends amongst Seniors and Enhancing Support for Them
what_it_is: Suicide Trends amongst Seniors and Enhancing Support for Them

sections.label: Suicide and senior isolation questions
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Health about suicide numbers, seniors aged 60 and above, those living alone, depression diagnoses, and pandemic support programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the number of people who have committed suicide or attempted suicide last year; (b) how many are aged 60 and above; (c) how many of such seniors are living alone; (d) how many of such seniors are diagnosed with depression prior to suicide or attempted suicide; and (e) what are the resources and programmes put in place during the pandemic to address the likely causes of such suicides and prevent the suicide rates from increasing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health in light of the Ministry's reply of 6 January 2020 on multi-pronged interventions to support seniors (a) how effective have these initiatives been in reducing elderly suicide; and (b) how is the Ministry working towards improving existing initiatives to cushion the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on our socially isolated elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) in light of a 2016 report on how 47,000 seniors aged 65 and above live by themselves, whether that figure has changed and, if so, by how much; and (b) in light of survey results showing lower social satisfaction levels for senior citizens during the circuit breaker period, whether the Ministry plans to enhance existing support mechanisms for the isolated elderly in the next two to three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The number of attempted suicide cases was about 1,000 in 2019.

sections.label: Seniors living alone increase
sections.summary: Singapore residents aged 65 and above living alone rose from 47,000 in 2016 to 67,600 in 2019, or 9.7% to 11.6% of that population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The number of Singapore residents aged 65 years and above who live alone has increased from 47,000 in 2016 to 67,600 in 2019, representing 9.7% and 11.6% of our resident population aged 65 years and above respectively.

sections.label: New eldercare centre service model
sections.summary: A new eldercare centre service model will be rolled out from May 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: From May 2021, we will be rolling out a new eldercare centre service model.

sections.label: SGO engagement with unsupported seniors
sections.summary: SGO engaged about 21,000 seniors with little or no social support during the circuit breaker through weekly or fortnightly calls.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: SGO also engaged about 21,000 seniors who have little or no social support during the circuit breaker period through weekly or fortnightly calls to monitor their well-being.
